v.t: Do we begin again to commend ourselves? or need we, as some others, epistles of commendation to you, or letters of commendation from you?

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, an apostle (2 Cor 1:1).

v.t: Ye are our epistle written in our hearts, known and read of all men:

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, an apostle (2 Cor 1:1).

v.t: Forasmuch as ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ ministered by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, an apostle (2 Cor 1:1).
tm.ot: Closely echoes Exod 31:18 (9 reader votes, OpenBible.info).

v.t: And such trust have we through Christ to God-ward:

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, an apostle (2 Cor 1:1).

v.t: Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency is of God;

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, an apostle (2 Cor 1:1).

v.t: Who also hath made us able ministers of the new testament; not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, an apostle (2 Cor 1:1).

v.t: But if the ministration of death, written and engraven in stones, was glorious, so that the children of Israel could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance; which glory was to be done away:

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, an apostle (2 Cor 1:1).

v.t: How shall not the ministration of the spirit be rather glorious?

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, an apostle (2 Cor 1:1).

v.t: For if the ministration of condemnation be glory, much more doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, an apostle (2 Cor 1:1).

v.t: For even that which was made glorious had no glory in this respect, by reason of the glory that excelleth.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, an apostle (2 Cor 1:1).

v.t: For if that which is done away was glorious, much more that which remaineth is glorious.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, an apostle (2 Cor 1:1).

v.t: Seeing then that we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech:

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, an apostle (2 Cor 1:1).

v.t: And not as Moses, which put a vail over his face, that the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished:

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, an apostle (2 Cor 1:1).
tm.ot: Closely echoes Exod 34:33 (11 reader votes, OpenBible.info).

v.t: But their minds were blinded: for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which vail is done away in Christ.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, an apostle (2 Cor 1:1).

v.t: But even unto this day, when Moses is read, the vail is upon their heart.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, an apostle (2 Cor 1:1).

v.t: Nevertheless when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, an apostle (2 Cor 1:1).

v.t: Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, an apostle (2 Cor 1:1).
tm.ot: Closely echoes Isa 61:1 (42 reader votes, OpenBible.info).

v.t: But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, an apostle (2 Cor 1:1).
